title: Stage residence time heatmap investigation
content:
Summary:
This note collects our focused investigation into per-stage residence times observed in end-to-end traces for the serving runtime. Goal: create a compact, reproducible playbook and set of hypotheses for regressions seen in the last two weeks (spike window 2024-10-10 -> 2024-10-15). The emphasis is on distributional shifts (p50/p95/p99) and stage-level heatmap visualization findings.

Dataset & sampling:
- Sources: production traces sampled via rt-tracer (trace-sampler v2) at 0.5% global, plus targeted 100% sampling for the /generate-long route during the incident window.
- Workloads: mixed (chat-left, long-batch-gen); median prompt length ~180 tokens, top 5% > 1.8k tokens.
- Synthetic repros: loadgen-run-2024-10-24 configured to reproduce the p95 regression with 50 concurrent clients, seq_len=1024, model=xr-large-8q.

Aggregate numbers (observed during spike window):
- End-to-end latency (server-side): p50=82ms, p95=284ms, p99=920ms (baseline: p50=60ms, p95=190ms, p99=420ms).

Per-stage breakdown (median and tail patterns):
- Router (auth+routing): p50=6ms, p95=12ms, p99=35ms. Stable.
- Tokenizer: p50=1.5ms, p95=4.6ms, p99=11ms. Minor noise.
- KV-cache lookup & merge: p50=8ms, p95=42ms, p99=310ms. Major contributor to p99.
- Kernel (attention + matmul): p50=48ms, p95=120ms, p99=220ms. Elevated but not sole cause.
- Postprocess (decoding, detokenize): p50=6ms, p95=18ms, p99=45ms. Small.
- Network egress (downstream clients): p50=12ms, p95=28ms, p99=60ms. Some region-specific tail.

Key observations from trace heatmap overlay (see attached heatmap screenshots in linked PR):
1) KV-cache stage shows concentrated, long-tailed residence times aligned with cache-miss spikes. Cross-check revealed increased cache eviction activity on hosts with mixed-model tenancy.
2) Kernel stage tail correlates with longer sequences but amplifies when concurrent batch size > 8 and when quantized kernels fallback to slower code path (observed in 3 hosts running older runtime build).
3) Router and tokenizer consistently small; they are not amplifying the tail.
4) A subset of traces show rapid oscillation: short kernel time followed by long KV-cache pauses, suggesting contention on the KV-IO path rather than compute starvation.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A. Cross-tenant KV cache eviction thrashing (mixed models) causes expensive rebuilds and remote fetches — explains high p99 at KV stage.
B. Fallback to reference kernels on older runtime builds combined with larger batches increases kernel execution variance — explains elevated p95 at kernel.
C. Network congestion in eu-west region for certain AZs increases egress tail; secondary effect.

Tests performed:
- Controlled repro with dedicated-only tenancy (no mixed models) reduced KV-cache p99 from ~310ms -> ~60ms.
- Rolling upgrade of 3 nodes to runtime v1.12.4 (optimized kernels) reduced kernel p95 by ~25% in loadgen runs.
- Forced cache-warm runs (pre-populate prefix cache) cut p99 overall by ~20%.

Immediate action items (short term):
- 48h: Schedule eviction-policy tweak (TTL increase for hot keys) on experiment fleet; monitor KV-cache miss rate. Owner: Aisha.
- 72h: Backfill critical hosts to runtime v1.12.4 (hotpath kernels). Owner: Miguel.
- 1 week: Add a targeted trace-sampler rule to capture 100% of /generate-long traces for any host reporting KV-cache > 120ms. Owner: Evan.

Longer-term proposals:
- Introduce per-tenant cache partitioning for Dedicated mode to avoid cross-tenant thrash (product impact: memory overhead vs tail reduction).
- Kernel auto-detect and per-request hints to choose quantized vs fallback paths earlier in the pipeline to avoid late-path stalls.
- Heatmap dashboard: add stage-residence heatmap with selectable percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and correlation lines for cache-miss rate and batch size.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Root cause of eviction spikes: is it memory pressure from other system processes or a change in eviction policy? Need host-level mem/cgroups audit.
- Are some prompt patterns (prefix reuse across tenants) causing cache churn? Need longer-term prompt fingerprinting telemetry (privacy-safe).

Notes and reproducibility steps (short):
1) checkout serving-runtime@investigation/kv-evict-2024
2) run tools/loadgen --config loadgen-run-2024-10-24 --concurrency 50 --seq 1024 --model xr-large-8q
3) collect traces with rt-tracer dump --filter route=/generate-long --out repro-traces.json
4) run python tools/trace_heatmap.py repro-traces.json --percentiles 50,95,99 --stages kv,kernel,router --out heatmap.png

Appendix (quick trace examples):
- trace_id: f2d9c7a4 (kv p99=412ms, kernel=180ms, end-to-end=1120ms)
- trace_id: 9b1a5c33 (kv p50=12ms, kernel p95=140ms, e2e=360ms)

If reviewers want, I can attach the loadgen scripts and a compact set of sampled traces (sanitized) to the linked PR.

Next review: sync with SRE + infra (Ravi) to confirm host-level metrics and with product to scope per-tenant partitioning tradeoffs.

Action owners: Evan (this doc), Aisha (eviction tweak), Miguel (runtime roll), Ravi (host audit), Janelle (dashboard mock).

-- end of note --
